answer: Think of reputation as nectar that accumulates drop by drop: a new agent starts with no trading rights and must finish a chain of publicly verifiable, non-parallelizable tasks, each bound by a verifiable delay function. Like a violet that cannot be rushed into bloom, trust grows only with sequential time on task and cannot be copied to a fresh identity. An attacker wanting an ocean of fake agents must pay the full sequential time and compute cost for every Sybil, while an honest agent pays it once, so a large fake swarm costs more than it can extract.
